topomer.note: 42 of 361 molecules can be cut at the framework

findings.text: 98 chemotype(s); the largest holds 38 of 361 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 18 heavy atoms, about 75% of a typical molecule, and 12% of the set can be cut at it
the 18 shared framework atoms sit 0.1 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (50 of 361 carry them)
the chosen attenuation 5 is at the top of the grid: the search needed a value it was not offered, so widen it before believing the model
the aligned model is +0.280 in q2 against counts (95% interval +0.177 to +0.374) -- the frame does better than counts
the aligned model is -0.010 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.077 to +0.049) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is -0.088 in q2 against topomer (95% interval -0.412 to +0.223) -- cutting the molecules and posing the pieces by rule does as well as the frame, on the molecules that can be cut
the aligned model is +0.469 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval +0.367 to +0.567) -- the geometry adds something

why: the frame gains nothing over invariant, which needs no alignment to curate and cannot be done wrongly
